# `prok-binning`

```{image} ../_static/pipeline_prok-binning.svg
:width: 100%
:class: no-scaled-link
:align: center
```

The prokaryotic binning module provides a robust, standardized framework for recovering Metagenome-Assembled Genomes (MAGs), functioning as a vital complement to the primary viral analysis within vOMIX-MEGA. The workflow initiates with the alignment of assembly contigs to paired-end cleaned fastq files utilizing the high-speed aligner `strobealign`. Researchers may subsequently choose between two distinct binning strategies: a consensus-based approach employing `MetaBat2`, `MaxBin`, and `CONCOCT`, which is subsequently integrated and refined via `DAS Tool` to maximize bin quality, or an accelerated, GPU-dependent approach utilizing `VAMB` for high-throughput recovery.

Following bin reconstruction, each MAG undergoes rigorous quality assessment for completeness and contamination using `CheckM2`. High-quality bins are subsequently dereplicated using `galah` to eliminate redundancy within the dataset. Finally, the taxonomic classification of each prokaryotic bin is determined using the `GTDB-Tk v2` toolkit, ensuring consistent and phylogenetically accurate identification of the recovered genomes.

## Quick Run

::::{tab-set}
:::{tab-item} Sample List

**`Conda`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="prok-binning" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`Apptainer`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="prok-binning" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Conda)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="prok-binning" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Apptainer)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="prok-binning" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

:::
::::

``` {admonition} Dry Run
:class: Tip
Use the `-n` flag with your command to perform a dry-run first, listing all analyses that will be performed 
```

## Configuration

- **`humann-params`:** Additional software parameters directed to the HUMAnN functional annotation pipeline. (default: "--remove-temp-output")

## Outputs

```bash
binning/prok
├── output
│   ├── clusters.tsv
│   ├── drep
│   ├── no-drep
│   └── taxonomy
├── assemblies
│   ├── assemblyA
│   ├── assemblyB
├── samples
│   ├── SampleA_assemblyA
│   ├── SampleB_assemblyA
│   └── SampleC_assemblyB
├── benchmarks
├── logs
└── tmp
```

The main output from this module is the assembly file `final.contigs.fa` which includes the final contigs generated by `megahit` or `SPAdes`. These contigs will be used for many steps in downstream analysis.
